\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Zk BLR}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.BLR.ZkBLR
\section{Overview}

This module formalizes the Blum–Luby–Rubinfeld (BLR) linearity test over
$\mathbb{Z}_k^n$.  A function $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is
\emph{linear} if $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x,y$, or equivalently if it
is a dot-product character $x \mapsto s \cdot x$ for some coefficient vector
$s$.  The module proves completeness (linear functions are always accepted)
and soundness bounds: if $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from every linear function,
the acceptance probability is at most
$1 - \tfrac{\varphi(k)}{k}(1-\cos(2\pi/k))\varepsilon$,
specialising for prime $p$ to $1 - \tfrac{p-1}{p}(1-\cos(2\pi/p))\varepsilon$.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Linearity predicate]
\lean{ZkBLR.is_linear}
\label{ZkBLR.is_linear}
\leanok
\uses{ZkFourier.ZkVec}
A function $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is \emph{linear} if
$f(x+y) = f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Lift to roots of unity]
\lean{ZkBLR.lift_omega}
\label{ZkBLR.lift_omega}
\leanok
\uses{ZkFourier.ZkFun, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.toOmega}
Given $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$, the lifted function
$\widetilde{f} : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{C}$ is defined by
$\widetilde{f}(x) = \omega_k^{f(x)}$, where $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Hamming distance between functions]
\lean{ZkBLR.zk_dist}
\label{ZkBLR.zk_dist}
\leanok
\uses{ZkFourier.ZkVec}
The distance between $f, g : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is the
fraction of inputs on which they disagree:
\[
  \mathrm{dist}(f,g) \;=\; \Pr_{x}[f(x) \ne g(x)]
  \;=\; \frac{1}{k^n}\#\{x : f(x)\ne g(x)\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[$\varepsilon$-far from linear]
\lean{ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear}
\label{ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.is_linear, ZkBLR.zk_dist, ZkFourier.ZkVec}
A function $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is
\emph{$\varepsilon$-far from linear} if $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$ and
$\mathrm{dist}(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$ for every linear function
$g : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Linear functions as dot-product characters]
\lean{ZkBLR.linear_iff_character}
\label{ZkBLR.linear_iff_character}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.is_linear, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.zkDot, ZkFourier.zkDot_add_right}
\difficulty{6}
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and a dimension $n$, and let $f : (\bbz/k\bbz)^n \to
\bbz/k\bbz$ be any function. Then $f$ is linear — that is, $f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y)$ for
all $x, y \in (\bbz/k\bbz)^n$ — if and only if there is a vector $s \in (\bbz/k\bbz)^n$
with $f(x) = s \cdot x = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} s_i x_i$ for every $x$, all sums taken modulo
$k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Canonical linear character]
\lean{ZkBLR.linear_character}
\label{ZkBLR.linear_character}
\leanok
\uses{ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.zkDot}
For $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$, the \emph{linear character} $\chi_s :
\mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is the dot-product function
$\chi_s(x) = s \cdot x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Normalized function]
\lean{ZkBLR.normalized}
\label{ZkBLR.normalized}
\leanok
\uses{ZkFourier.ZkVec}
A function $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is \emph{normalized} if
$f(0) = 0$.  Every linear function is automatically normalized.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Normalization operator]
\lean{ZkBLR.normalize}
\label{ZkBLR.normalize}
\leanok
\uses{ZkFourier.ZkVec}
The \emph{normalization} of $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is the
function $(\mathrm{normalize}\,f)(x) = f(x) - f(0)$, which satisfies
$(\mathrm{normalize}\,f)(0) = 0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Normalization vanishes at the origin]
\lean{ZkBLR.normalize_zero}
\label{ZkBLR.normalize_zero}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.normalize, ZkFourier.ZkVec}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f : (\bbz/k\bbz)^n \to \bbz/k\bbz$ be any function on the $n$-dimensional space
over $\bbz/k\bbz$, and let its normalization be $(\mathrm{normalize}\,f)(x) = f(x) -
f(0)$. Then this normalization vanishes at the origin: $(\mathrm{normalize}\,f)(0) = 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Linear functions are normalized]
\lean{ZkBLR.linear_normalized}
\label{ZkBLR.linear_normalized}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.is_linear, ZkBLR.normalized, ZkFourier.ZkVec}
\difficulty{1}
Let $k \ge 1$ and $n$ be natural numbers, and let $f : (\bbz/k\bbz)^n \to \bbz/k\bbz$ be
a linear function, meaning $f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y)$ for all $x, y \in (\bbz/k\bbz)^n$.
Then $f$ is normalized: $f(0) = 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[$\varepsilon$-far from linear, normalized version]
\lean{ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized}
\label{ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.is_linear, ZkBLR.normalized, ZkBLR.zk_dist, ZkFourier.ZkVec}
A function $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ satisfies
\texttt{ZkBLR.epsilon\_far\_from\_linear\_normalized} with parameter $\varepsilon$
if $f$ is normalized ($f(0)=0$), $0\le\varepsilon\le 1$, and
$\mathrm{dist}(f,g)\ge\varepsilon$ for every linear $g$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Real part of a nontrivial root of unity]
\lean{ZkBLR.re_toOmega_le_re_rootOfUnity}
\label{ZkBLR.re_toOmega_le_re_rootOfUnity}
\leanok
\uses{ZkFourier.rootOfUnity, ZkFourier.toOmega}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k \ge 2$ and write $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i / k}$ for the primitive $k$-th root of
unity. For every nonzero $a \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\omega_k^{\,a}\right) \le \cos\!\left(\frac{2\pi}{k}\right),
\]
where $\omega_k^{\,a}$ denotes $\omega_k$ raised to the canonical representative of $a$
in $\{0, 1, \ldots, k-1\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Upper bound on the real part of a Fourier coefficient]
\lean{ZkBLR.re_fourier_coeff_upper_bound}
\label{ZkBLR.re_fourier_coeff_upper_bound}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.lift_omega, ZkBLR.linear_character, ZkBLR.re_toOmega_le_re_rootOfUnity, ZkBLR.zk_dist, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.char_s, ZkFourier.expectation, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff, ZkFourier.inner_product, ZkFourier.rootOfUnity, ZkFourier.toOmega, ZkFourier.toOmega_add, ZkFourier.toOmega_neg, ZkFourier.zkDot}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k \ge 2$ and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$, with lift $\widetilde{f}(x)
= \omega_k^{f(x)}$ where $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$. Then for every frequency $s \in
\mathbb{Z}_k^n$, the real part of the Fourier coefficient of $\widetilde{f}$ at $s$ is
bounded above by
\[
  \operatorname{Re}\bigl[\widehat{\widetilde{f}}(s)\bigr]
  \;\le\;
  1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\,\mathrm{dist}(f,\chi_s),
\]
where $\chi_s(x) = s\cdot x$ is the linear character and $\mathrm{dist}(f,\chi_s)$ is
the fraction of inputs $x$ on which $f(x) \ne s\cdot x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier bound for functions far from linear]
\lean{ZkBLR.re_epsilon_far_bounds_fourier}
\label{ZkBLR.re_epsilon_far_bounds_fourier}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized, ZkBLR.is_linear, ZkBLR.lift_omega, ZkBLR.linear_character, ZkBLR.re_fourier_coeff_upper_bound, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff, ZkFourier.zkDot_add_right}
\difficulty{3}
Fix an integer $k \ge 2$ and let $f : \bbz_k^n \to \bbz_k$ be $\varepsilon$-far from
linear in the normalized sense: that is, $f(0) = 0$, the parameter satisfies $0 \le
\varepsilon \le 1$, and $\dist(f, g) \ge \varepsilon$ for every linear $g : \bbz_k^n \to
\bbz_k$. Write $\widetilde{f}(x) = \omega_k^{f(x)}$ for the lift of $f$ to the unit
circle, where $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$, and let $\widehat{\widetilde{f}}(s)$ denote its
Fourier coefficient at frequency $s$. Then for every $s \in \bbz_k^n$,
\[
  \operatorname{Re}\bigl[\widehat{\widetilde{f}}(s)\bigr]
  \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\,\varepsilon.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[$j$-twisted lift to roots of unity]
\lean{ZkBLR.lift_omega_j}
\label{ZkBLR.lift_omega_j}
\leanok
\uses{ZkFourier.ZkFun, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.toOmega}
For $j \in \mathbb{Z}_k$, the $j$-twisted lift of
$f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is
$\widetilde{f}_j(x) = \omega_k^{j \cdot f(x)}$.
The case $j=1$ recovers \texttt{ZkBLR.lift\_omega}; the case $j=0$ gives the
constant function $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[BLR acceptance probability]
\lean{ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob}
\label{ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob}
\leanok
\uses{ZkFourier.ZkVec}
The BLR acceptance probability of $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ is
\[
  \Pr_{x,y}\bigl[f(x+y) = f(x)+f(y)\bigr]
  \;=\; \frac{1}{k^{2n}}
    \sum_{x,y\in\mathbb{Z}_k^n}
    \mathbf{1}\bigl[f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)\bigr].
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Completeness of the BLR linearity test]
\lean{ZkBLR.BLR_completeness}
\label{ZkBLR.BLR_completeness}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob, ZkBLR.is_linear, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.card_ZkVec}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$, and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ be a linear
function, meaning $f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$. Then the BLR
acceptance probability of $f$ equals $1$; that is,
\[
  \Pr_{x,y}\bigl[f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y)\bigr] = 1,
\]
where $x$ and $y$ range independently and uniformly over $\mathbb{Z}_k^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Orthogonality sum for additive characters mod $k$]
\lean{ZkBLR.geom_sum_toOmega_dual}
\label{ZkBLR.geom_sum_toOmega_dual}
\leanok
\statementsource{boolean-ch01-fourier-blr}{pdf-cdca27e1b5fd-p006-b005}
\uses{ZkFourier.geom_sum_toOmega, ZkFourier.toOmega}
\difficulty{1}
Let $k \ge 1$ and write $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$ for the primitive $k$-th root of
unity. For each $a \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
  \sum_{j \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}} \omega_k^{\,j a}
  \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    k & \text{if } a = 0, \\
    0 & \text{otherwise,}
  \end{cases}
\]
where each exponent $ja \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ is taken via its canonical
representative in $\{0, 1, \ldots, k-1\}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indicator as a character sum]
\lean{ZkBLR.indicator_eq_char_sum_re}
\label{ZkBLR.indicator_eq_char_sum_re}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.geom_sum_toOmega_dual, ZkFourier.toOmega}
\difficulty{2}
Let $k \ge 1$ and write $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$ for the primitive $k$-th root of
unity. For every $a \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$,
\[
\mathbf{1}[a = 0] \;=\; \frac{1}{k}\,\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\sum_{j \in
\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}} \omega_k^{\,ja}\right),
\]
where the exponent $ja$ is computed in $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ and then lifted to its
canonical representative in $\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, and the left-hand side equals $1$ when
$a = 0$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Parseval identity for the twisted lift]
\lean{ZkBLR.parseval_lift_omega_j}
\label{ZkBLR.parseval_lift_omega_j}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.lift_omega_j, ZkFourier.L2_norm_sq, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.card_ZkVec, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff, ZkFourier.norm_toOmega, ZkFourier.parseval_identity, ZkFourier.toOmega}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$ be integers, and write $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$. Fix $j \in
\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ and an arbitrary function $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to
\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$, and let $\widetilde{f}_j : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{C}$ be
the $j$-twisted lift given by $\widetilde{f}_j(x) = \omega_k^{\,j\cdot f(x)}$, with
Fourier coefficients $\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)$ indexed by the frequencies $s \in
\mathbb{Z}_k^n$. Then
\[
\sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n} \bigl\lvert \widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s) \bigr\rvert^{2} =
1.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Triple-product identity for the twisted lift]
\lean{ZkBLR.triple_product_fourier}
\label{ZkBLR.triple_product_fourier}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.lift_omega_j, ZkFourier.ZkFun, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.char_s, ZkFourier.char_s_add, ZkFourier.expectation, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff, ZkFourier.fourier_expansion, ZkFourier.inner_product}
\difficulty{6}
Fix $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$, and work over the group $\mathbb{Z}_k^n =
(\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^n$ with primitive $k$-th root of unity $\omega_k = e^{2\pi
i/k}$. Given $j \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ and a map $f \colon \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to
\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$, let $F(x) = \omega_k^{\,j\cdot f(x)}$ be its $j$-twisted lift,
and for $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$ let $\widehat{F}(s) =
\mathbb{E}_x\!\big[F(x)\,\overline{\omega_k^{\,s\cdot x}}\big]$ be its Fourier
coefficient, where $s\cdot x = \sum_{i} s_i x_i \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ and
$\mathbb{E}$ denotes the uniform average over $\mathbb{Z}_k^n$. Then the triple-product
expectation over independent uniform $x,y$ equals a cubic sum of the Fourier
coefficients:
\[
  \mathbb{E}_x\,\mathbb{E}_y\!\left[F(x+y)\,\overline{F(x)}\,\overline{F(y)}\right]
= \sum_{s\in\mathbb{Z}_k^n} \bigl\lvert
\widehat{F}(s)\bigr\rvert^2\,\overline{\widehat{F}(s)}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[BLR acceptance probability as a Fourier sum]
\lean{ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob_eq_fourier_sum}
\label{ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob_eq_fourier_sum}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob, ZkBLR.indicator_eq_char_sum_re, ZkBLR.lift_omega_j, ZkBLR.triple_product_fourier, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.expectation, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff, ZkFourier.toOmega, ZkFourier.toOmega_add, ZkFourier.toOmega_neg}
\difficulty{6}
Let $k \ge 1$, and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$. For each $j \in
\mathbb{Z}_k$ let $\widetilde{f}_j(x) = \omega_k^{\,j\,f(x)}$ denote the $j$-twisted
lift of $f$, and write $\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)$ for its Fourier coefficient at
frequency $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$. Then the BLR acceptance probability of $f$ admits the
representation
\[
  \Pr_{x,y}\bigl[f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)\bigr]
  = \frac{1}{k}
    \sum_{j\in\mathbb{Z}_k}\;
    \sum_{s\in\mathbb{Z}_k^n}
    \bigl|\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)\bigr|^2\,
    \operatorname{Re}\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s),
\]
where $|\cdot|$ is the complex modulus and $\operatorname{Re}$ the real part.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Zero-twisted lift contributes one to the Fourier sum]
\lean{ZkBLR.lift_omega_j_zero_contribution}
\label{ZkBLR.lift_omega_j_zero_contribution}
\leanok

Write $\widetilde{f}_0(x) = \omega_k^{\,0 \cdot f(x)}$ for the $0$-twisted lift of $f$
(equivalently, the constant function $1$), and let $\widehat{\widetilde{f}_0}(s)$ denote
its Fourier coefficient at frequency $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$. Then

  \sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n}
    \bigl|\widehat{\widetilde{f}_0}(s)\bigr|^2 \,
    \operatorname{Re}\widehat{\widetilde{f}_0}(s) = 1,
\]
where $|\cdot|$ is the complex modulus.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Weighted Fourier sum bounded by one]
\lean{ZkBLR.weighted_fourier_sum_le_one}
\label{ZkBLR.weighted_fourier_sum_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.lift_omega_j, ZkBLR.parseval_lift_omega_j, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k \ge 1$ and $n$ be integers, fix $j \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ and a function $f
: \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$, and let $\widetilde{f}_j(x) =
\omega_k^{\,j\,f(x)}$ be its $j$-twisted lift, with Fourier coefficients
$\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)$ indexed by frequencies $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$. Then
\[
  \sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n}
    \bigl\lvert \widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s) \bigr\rvert^{2}\,

where $\lvert\cdot\rvert$ denotes the complex modulus and $\operatorname{Re}$ the real

\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cube-sum of Fourier coefficients bounded by the maximum]
\lean{ZkBLR.cube_sum_bound_by_max}
\label{ZkBLR.cube_sum_bound_by_max}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.lift_omega, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $p$ be a prime, let $n \ge 0$, and let $f : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$ be a function,
whose lift to roots of unity is $\widetilde{f}(x) = \omega_p^{f(x)}$ with $\omega_p =
e^{2\pi i/p}$. Write $\widehat{\widetilde{f}}(s)$ for the Fourier coefficient of
$\widetilde{f}$ at frequency $s \in \bbz_p^n$. If $A \in \bbr$ is such that
$\bigl\|\widehat{\widetilde{f}}(s)\bigr\| \le A$ for every $s \in \bbz_p^n$, then

  \sum_{s \in \bbz_p^n} \bigl\|\widehat{\widetilde{f}}(s)\bigr\|^3
  \;\le\;

\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier coefficient bound for a twisted lift of an $\varepsilon$-far function]
\lean{ZkBLR.re_fourier_coeff_lift_omega_j_bound}
\label{ZkBLR.re_fourier_coeff_lift_omega_j_bound}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized, ZkBLR.lift_omega_j, ZkBLR.re_epsilon_far_bounds_fourier, ZkBLR.zk_dist, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff}

Let $p$ be a prime, let $n \ge 0$, and write $\omega_p = e^{2\pi i/p}$ for the primitive
$p$-th root of unity. Let $f : \bbz_p^{\,n} \to \bbz_p$ be normalized ($f(0)=0$) and
$\varepsilon$-far from linear, meaning $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$ and $\Pr_x[f(x)\ne
g(x)] \ge \varepsilon$ for every additive homomorphism $g : \bbz_p^{\,n} \to \bbz_p$.
Fix $j \in \bbz_p$ with $j \ne 0$, and for $s \in \bbz_p^{\,n}$ let $\widehat{h}(s) =
\E_x\bigl[h(x)\,\omega_p^{-\,s\cdot x}\bigr]$ denote the Fourier coefficient of a
function $h : \bbz_p^{\,n} \to \bbc$ at frequency $s$, where $s\cdot x = \sum_{i} s_i
x_i \in \bbz_p$. Then the $j$-twisted lift $\widetilde{f}_j(x) = \omega_p^{\,j\,f(x)}$
satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Re}\,\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s) \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 -
\cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\,\varepsilon
\]
for every $s \in \bbz_p^{\,n}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Weighted Fourier bound for the twisted lift of a far-from-linear function]
\lean{ZkBLR.weighted_sum_lift_omega_j_bound}
\label{ZkBLR.weighted_sum_lift_omega_j_bound}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized, ZkBLR.lift_omega_j, ZkBLR.parseval_lift_omega_j, ZkBLR.re_fourier_coeff_lift_omega_j_bound, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $p$ be prime and let $f : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$ be normalized, meaning $f(0) = 0$,
and $\varepsilon$-far from linear: $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$ and $\mathrm{dist}(f,g) \ge
\varepsilon$ for every linear function $g : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$, where $\mathrm{dist}$
denotes the fraction of inputs on which the two functions disagree. Fix a nonzero $j \in
\bbz_p$ and let $\widetilde{f}_j(x) = \omega_p^{\,j\, f(x)}$ be the associated
$j$-twisted lift, with $\omega_p = e^{2\pi i / p}$, and write
$\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)$ for its Fourier coefficient at frequency $s$. Then
\[
\sum_{s \in \bbz_p^n} \bigl|\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)\bigr|^2
\,\operatorname{Re}\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)
  \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\varepsilon .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[BLR soundness over a prime field]
\lean{ZkBLR.BLR_soundness}
\label{ZkBLR.BLR_soundness}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob, ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob_eq_fourier_sum, ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized, ZkBLR.lift_omega_j_zero_contribution, ZkBLR.weighted_sum_lift_omega_j_bound, ZkFourier.ZkVec}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ be prime and fix $n \ge 0$. Let $f : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$ be a normalized
function (so $f(0)=0$), and let $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$ be such that $f$ is
$\varepsilon$-far from every linear map, meaning $\mathrm{dist}(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$
for every linear $g : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$, where $\mathrm{dist}(f,g) = \Pr_x[f(x) \ne
g(x)]$. Then the BLR acceptance probability of $f$ satisfies
\[
  \Pr_{x,y}\bigl[f(x+y) = f(x)+f(y)\bigr]
  \;\le\; 1 - \frac{p-1}{p}\,\bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\,\varepsilon,
\]
where $x,y$ range uniformly and independently over $\bbz_p^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[$\varepsilon$-farness preserved under unit scaling]
\lean{ZkBLR.unit_mul_epsilon_far}
\label{ZkBLR.unit_mul_epsilon_far}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized, ZkBLR.zk_dist, ZkFourier.ZkVec}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f : \bbz_k^n \to \bbz_k$ be a normalized function that is $\varepsilon$-far from
linear, meaning $f(0) = 0$, $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, and $\dist(f, g) \ge \varepsilon$
for every linear $g : \bbz_k^n \to \bbz_k$. Then for any unit $j \in (\bbz_k)^\times$,
the scaled function $x \mapsto j \cdot f(x)$ is again normalized and $\varepsilon$-far
from linear.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Real-part bound for a unit-twisted lift]
\lean{ZkBLR.re_fourier_coeff_lift_omega_j_unit_bound}
\label{ZkBLR.re_fourier_coeff_lift_omega_j_unit_bound}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized, ZkBLR.lift_omega_j, ZkBLR.re_epsilon_far_bounds_fourier, ZkBLR.unit_mul_epsilon_far, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff}
\difficulty{2}
Let $k \ge 2$ and let $f : \bbz_k^n \to \bbz_k$ be normalized and $\varepsilon$-far from
linear, meaning that $f(0) = 0$, that $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, and that $\dist(f,g)
\ge \varepsilon$ for every linear $g : \bbz_k^n \to \bbz_k$ (where $\dist$ is the
fraction of inputs on which two functions disagree). Fix a unit $j \in
(\bbz/k\bbz)^\times$ and a frequency $s \in \bbz_k^n$, and let $\widetilde{f}_j(x) =
\omega_k^{\,j\,f(x)}$ be the corresponding $j$-twisted lift, with $\omega_k = e^{2\pi
i/k}$. Then the Fourier coefficient of $\widetilde{f}_j$ at $s$ has real part bounded by
\[
\operatorname{Re}\,\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s) \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 -
\cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\,\varepsilon .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A weighted Fourier-coefficient bound for a unit-twisted lift]
\lean{ZkBLR.weighted_sum_unit_bound}
\label{ZkBLR.weighted_sum_unit_bound}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized, ZkBLR.lift_omega_j, ZkBLR.parseval_lift_omega_j, ZkBLR.re_fourier_coeff_lift_omega_j_unit_bound, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k \ge 2$, and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ be normalized (that is,
$f(0) = 0$) and $\varepsilon$-far from linear for some $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$,
meaning that $\mathrm{dist}(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$ for every linear function $g :
\mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$. Then for every unit $j \in
(\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z})^\times$, the $j$-twisted lift $\widetilde{f}_j(x) =
\omega_k^{\,j\,f(x)}$ satisfies
\[
  \sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n}
    \bigl|\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)\bigr|^2 \,
    \operatorname{Re}\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)
  \;\le\; 1 - \bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\varepsilon,
\]
where $\widehat{\widetilde{f}_j}(s)$ denotes the Fourier coefficient of
$\widetilde{f}_j$ at frequency $s$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[BLR soundness over $\mathbb{Z}_k$]
\lean{ZkBLR.BLR_soundness_general}
\label{ZkBLR.BLR_soundness_general}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob, ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob_eq_fourier_sum, ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized, ZkBLR.lift_omega_j, ZkBLR.weighted_fourier_sum_le_one, ZkBLR.weighted_sum_unit_bound, ZkFourier.ZkVec, ZkFourier.fourier_coeff}
\difficulty{6}
Let $k \ge 2$, and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ be normalized, so that
$f(0) = 0$. Fix a real number $\varepsilon$ with $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, and suppose
$f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from linear: for every linear function $g : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to
\mathbb{Z}_k$ (one satisfying $g(x+y) = g(x)+g(y)$ for all $x,y$), the fraction of
inputs on which $f$ and $g$ disagree is at least $\varepsilon$. Then the acceptance
probability of the BLR linearity test, taken over independent uniform $x, y \in
\mathbb{Z}_k^n$, obeys
\[
  \Pr_{x,y}\bigl[f(x+y) = f(x)+f(y)\bigr]
  \;\le\; 1 - \frac{\varphi(k)}{k}\bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/k)\bigr)\,\varepsilon,
\]
where $\varphi$ denotes Euler's totient function.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[BLR soundness over a prime field]
\lean{ZkBLR.BLR_soundness_prime}
\label{ZkBLR.BLR_soundness_prime}
\leanok
\uses{ZkBLR.BLR_accept_prob, ZkBLR.BLR_soundness_general, ZkBLR.epsilon_far_from_linear_normalized, ZkFourier.ZkVec}
\difficulty{2}
Let $p$ be prime and let $f : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$ be normalized, meaning $f(0) = 0$.
Fix $\varepsilon$ with $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, and suppose $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far
from linear: every linear function $g : \bbz_p^n \to \bbz_p$ (one satisfying $g(x+y) =
g(x)+g(y)$ for all $x,y$) has $\dist(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$, where $\dist(f,g) =
\Pr_x[f(x) \ne g(x)]$. Then the BLR acceptance probability of $f$ obeys
\[
  \Pr_{x,y}\bigl[f(x+y) = f(x)+f(y)\bigr]
  \;\le\; 1 - \frac{p-1}{p}\bigl(1 - \cos(2\pi/p)\bigr)\,\varepsilon,
\]
the probability being taken over $x,y$ drawn independently and uniformly from
$\bbz_p^n$.
\end{lemma}
